newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat meets Mubarak ahead of talks with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets Mubarak ahead of talks with Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Saturday ahead of peace talks with Israel expected to begin on Sunday, diplomats said.
The two men were expected to discuss the outcome of this week's Middle East crisis summit hosted by U.S. President Bill Clinton which Mubarak declined to attend.
Arafat flew to Cairo after meeting French President Jacques Chirac in Paris and Italian leaders in Naples.
Arafat has called for a European presence in Sunday's talks which will take place on the Israeli border with the self-rule Gaza Strip.

In Dublin, Italy and France are pressing a one-day informal European Union summit to reaffirm the 15-nation bloc's desire to play a role in rescuing the Middle East peace process dominated by the mediation efforts of the United States.

On Friday, France rapped Washington for the paltry results of the Washington summit, hastily called to halt the worst clashes in the Jewish state and self-rule areas since the Palestinians and Israel signed a peace deal in 1993.
Egypt, a broker of several rounds of Palestinian-Israeli negotiations, did not attend the summit because of what it called the intransigence of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Palestinian officials deemed the summit a failure. Its only concrete result was a continuation of Israeli-Palestinian talks from Sunday.
